title: Shedding of Deciduous Teeth
tocPath: APPROACH TO PATIENTS WITH EMERGENCY CONDITIONS

blocks.text: Phenomenon where deciduous/primary teeth are replaced by permanent teeth. This process occurring between ages of 5–12 years as a normal physiological change. Deciduous teeth should be left to fall out themselves unless the teeth are carious or there is any other indication. Parents should be counseled accordingly and be instructed to assist their children to loosen the already mobile teeth.

Often referred to as "Phase II" or comprehensive orthodontic correction, is the full-scale alignment of permanent teeth and the correction of bite relationships after early intervention (Phase I) or as a single-phase approach. Main goals include: Precise alignment of all permanent teeth, Correction of bite issues (overbite, underbite, crossbite) and achieving proper jaw harmony and long-term functional stability. This treatment should start when most permanent teeth (excluding wisdom teeth) are erupted (around ages 10–14 years).

Endodontic treatment or root canal treatment is a dental procedure used to repair and save a badly damaged or infected tooth. It involves removing the infected or damaged pulp from tooth’s root canals, cleaning and disinfecting the area, and then filling and sealing it. This procedure aims to eliminate infection and protect the tooth from future microbial invasion, ultimately saving the tooth from extraction.

blocks.text: An impacted tooth is a tooth which is still completely or partially covered by mucosa and bone for more than 2 years following its physiological eruption time. Although the prevalence varies from location to location and from tooth to tooth. Third molars (wisdom teeth) are the most prevalent impacted teeth followed by maxillary canine teeth.
